t1.text: 1 · The hook: email to first reveal

t2.text: 2 · The core path: twist to the ledger

t3.text: 3 · Threads: optional detours, pulled where the question arises

s_email.text: Readable in 20 seconds, one button. Magic link, no login. Subject: 'Your temps and contractors haven't been paid. Nobody will say why.' Preheader: 'A 6-minute scenario. Your first decision takes 2 minutes.'

s_scene.text: One screen, no scrolling. The nuance sits in the chips: weekly pay, fractional hours, some in IT, contract owned by HR.

s_d1.text: Commit first. Pick one or two before seeing anything. Combinations tell a different story from single choices.

s_hold.text: Only appears if B is picked. Mandatory, no reveal here. It feeds Reveal 1. B-choosers also get the thread chip "Are you owning this?" (T1).

s_r1.text: First payoff, about 2 minutes in. Shows only the hidden assumptions; gains and costs stay hidden. The flag on each card captures "I'd check this in my own organisation" in one tap.

s_twist.text: Double twist. Two thread chips attach to the exact lines that raise them: the clock (T3) and who should have checked (T2). Thread dots in the header show how many you have pulled.

s_d2.text: The menu is shaped by Decision 1. Saturday 14:00 chip leads to T4. Locking in goes to the flight recorder, not straight to the forecast.

s_pred.text: One tap. A small stake before the ledger appears, so the gap between guess and result makes people stop and reread.

s_r2.text: THE "WORTH MY TIME" LINE. A state, not a debrief. 5 rows on the surface, 2 behind a tap. Flag what you would take back; threads you pulled add rows here.

s_close.text: Safe exit. A mirror built from their own choices, the action they took back, a share prompt, then the soft door.

s_depth.text: Threads are optional, about a minute, same mechanic (choice, assumption, gain and cost). Each has its own mini-payoff. T1 to T4 attach to the screens named in the chips; T5 opens from a ledger row.

s_parked.text: Parked for later: replay, more threads, a lighter register test, slower reveals once trust is earned. Decide: whether the 30-day follow-up is promised on screen.

s_log.text: A forecast of your own behaviour, written before the reveal. First hour required, day and week optional. Skip has equal weight. Not a promise: it is what the replay compares against.

s_commit.text: One real-world action, chosen from what you flagged. A date and an opt-in 30-day follow-up email. The closing line mirrors it.
